# ADR-005 — Published terms and simulated payment

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Applies to** US-03  
**Basis** [Approved US-03 Draft 2](../../spec/US-03.md), [specification approval](../approvals/US-03-spec-approval.md), assessment pp. 2 and 8–9

## Context

[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves a country-scoped terms document and public read action. [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern. [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps quote state and payment in the browser, and [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) already gates editable Summary on valid Details and a freshly revalidated plan. The existing Angular 21.2 wizard has the Summary handoff and the Strapi 5.63 controller already serves Form and Plans through the same-origin proxy. US-03 needs a terms revision contract, a payment attempt that refreshes consent before it starts, and a terminal receipt that survives reload.

## Proposed decision

### Published terms contract

Create a Terms collection with Draft & Publish and one document per country. Use the existing country enum and a required, nonblank multiline plain-text body of at most 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Preserve the body as returned by Strapi, including paragraph breaks. Read only the published country document through the Document Service, selecting only country and body. Read up to two documents to detect duplicate publications and fail if either the country or body is invalid. Seed one fictitious, country-specific publication for Colombia and Chile in the existing startup workflow. Track seeding separately from Forms and Plans, skip countries with existing Terms documents during initial seeding, and preserve editorial changes and deliberate unpublication on subsequent starts. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status)

Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/terms` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing country parser and reject request query parameters. Project `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, revision, text }`. Define `revision` as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON tuple `[1, country, text]`, computed by Strapi from the projected values. It identifies the exact country text the user can accept. Publishing changed text changes its revision and republishing identical text keeps the revision. The shared `@quote/contract` decoder checks the envelope version, expected country, revision format and text bounds at the server and browser boundaries. Angular presents terms as text, preserving line breaks and treating markup as literal content. [Angular security](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)

| Outcome | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Valid published document | `200` with the terms envelope |
| Unexpected query parameters or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
| No published document | `404 TERMS_NOT_PUBLISHED` |
| Duplicate or invalid published configuration | `503 TERMS_UNAVAILABLE` |
| CMS retrieval failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |

Reuse the `{ error: { code } }` envelope and `Cache-Control: no-store` on handler outcomes. Extend the same-origin, GET-only proxy allowlist and add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readTerms` to the Public role alongside Form and Plans. Generated CRUD, draft and admin access, and write credentials stay outside the public contract. The terms request carries the country in the path and no quote, consent or payment data. The proxy bypasses caching as it does for Form and Plans. [HTTP caching](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html)

### Summary and consent

Extend the existing Summary handoff. Build a read-only review projection from the active country's validated, reconciled Details and freshly selected Plan. Use current field order, labels and option labels, the existing money formatter and the plan's final price. Mask the `identityDocument` value before it enters the review projection so both visible and accessible output use the same masked string. Apply Q-US03-01 to alphanumeric characters, preserving separators. Keep the raw value in the existing Details draft only. There is no additional form field or network contract for the review.

Read Terms on Summary entry and explicit retry through the existing `HttpClient` and signals pattern. Bind consent in memory to the active country, terms revision and the review snapshot. Compare snapshots by value using the current field identifiers, kinds and normalized values, and the selected plan ID and final money value. Navigation back to edit preserves Details and the plan candidate under their existing rules. A change to normalized quote data, plan, price or terms revision invalidates consent. Cancellation and generation checks prevent superseded responses from replacing active terms. Loading or failed terms reads leave the review available and prevent payment. [Angular HTTP requests](https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests)

### One simulated attempt and terminal recovery

1. The quote feature owns one attempt state per country. A single Pay command checks the live editable Summary prerequisites, consent and absence of a busy or completed payment. It synchronously reserves an attempt before requesting fresh country Terms. That reservation locks submission during both the refresh and the simulation. The attempt captures the country, active Summary generation, consent binding and the selected demo outcome.
2. Only the current attempt may act on the refresh result. Recheck the active country and Summary generation, current Details and plan validity, quote snapshot, and consent. A valid changed revision replaces the presented terms and clears consent. A failed or invalid read leaves a recoverable terms error. Both outcomes release the reservation without invoking the simulator. A matching revision advances directly to processing under the same reservation.
3. The local asynchronous simulator accepts only the captured Approved or Rejected outcome. Approved is the selector default. Outcome changes after reservation apply to a subsequent attempt. The simulator has no external side effects and takes no card, Details or plan data. Only the matching live attempt may settle. Rejection releases the lock with a retryable error and keeps the draft, selected plan and matching consent. A retry goes through the same Pay command and a fresh terms read. Leaving Summary, switching country or replacing the quote invalidates outstanding work. Cancel pending reads and ignore callbacks that can no longer settle. Browser Back or Forward cannot replay Pay.
4. Success creates one browser-generated opaque simulated quote number and commits an immutable terminal receipt once. Persist only the minimal completed receipt in a bounded, versioned country-scoped `sessionStorage` record alongside the existing draft and plan entries. Keep country and quote number in the receipt. Decode the record as untrusted input, rejecting oversized, unknown-version, malformed or wrong-country values. Consent and unfinished attempts stay in memory. After reload, an interrupted attempt therefore cannot resume or settle. The person returns through the existing Details and plan checks and can retry after current consent. If storage is unavailable, retain the same duplicate guard and receipt for the current page session under ADR-003. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)
5. A valid restored receipt is the terminal confirmation for the current country quote. On the Summary route, restore that confirmation without opening editable Summary or presenting live plan, price or terms as part of the receipt. CMS changes do not alter a settled result. History traversal and switching back to that country preserve the receipt and cannot make the same quote payable. Only an explicit start-new-quote reset under ADR-003 may clear that country's receipt, draft, plan and in-memory payment state. Clear the terminal lock last so a partial reset cannot silently reopen the completed quote. Editable Summary for an unfinished or explicitly reset quote still uses the live prerequisite redirects in ADR-004.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Embed Terms in Form Configuration or expose generated Strapi reads | Embedding ties independent publication schedules together. Generated reads widen the public surface. The dedicated action adds one bounded response and Public permission. |
| Use `updatedAt`, `publishedAt` or an editor-entered revision | Metadata can change while the displayed text is unchanged. Manual revisions can drift from text. The content fingerprint follows what the person reviews and accepts. |
| Trust terms from Summary entry or lock only once simulation begins | Entry-only terms can miss a published change. A later lock allows overlapping Pay refreshes. Reserving before the fresh read costs one terms request per eligible Pay attempt and closes that overlap. A CMS publication after the successful read may still occur while the local simulation runs. |
| Persist consent and unfinished attempts or require fresh CMS data to restore a receipt | Persisting in-flight state needs restoration rules and risks replay. Revalidating a historical receipt against current editorial data can erase access to a completed result. A minimal terminal record supports reload without reviving unfinished work or copying quote details. |
| Add a server-side payment endpoint | Server persistence could coordinate across tabs or devices. The approved simulator is local, so tab-scoped duplicate protection has no server or gateway dependency. |

## Verification

- Use AC-US03-01, AC-US03-02 and AC-US03-04 / T-US03-01, T-US03-02 and T-US03-04 to verify the review projection and same-country edit path in Colombia and Chile. Check that the full document is absent from the visible and accessible Summary.
- Use AC-US03-03 and AC-US03-09 / T-US03-03 and T-US03-11 to verify country-isolated published reads, revision changes and identical republishes, draft isolation, missing/invalid/unavailable terms, fresh Pay reads and consent invalidation. Verify the Public role and proxy allow only the intended content reads, and confirm a published terms edit reaches the running Angular build.
- Use AC-US03-05 through AC-US03-08 and AC-US03-10 / T-US03-05 through T-US03-09 to verify one attempt through both phases, deterministic Approved and Rejected in both countries, retry, late responses after navigation, and reload of interrupted and completed states. Check wrong-country and corrupt storage, memory fallback, and completed receipt recovery after rejected live prerequisites without opening editable Summary. T-US03-10 covers the full flow at project verification.

| Pattern | Design contract |
| --- | --- |
| Header and country selection | The global header shows product identity. The picker and recovery for unsupported routes offer links to supported countries. The URL sets the active country and its isolated quote state. Include a main landmark, skip link and unique heading. On wizard navigation, focus the new screen heading. |
| Progress track | An informational ordered list of Datos, Plan and Resumen, centered on desktop. Mark the current step with `aria-current="step"` and expose completed status as text to assistive technology. Use separate Back and Edit actions. |

| Field feedback | Neutral on initial render. Show the configured error on invalid blur or unsuccessful Continue. Update or clear it as touched values change. Set `aria-invalid` while showing the error and move focus to the first invalid field on Continue. |

**Status** Proposed · Pending human design approval

**Basis** [Approved US-03](../../spec/US-03.md), [ADR-005](../adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md) and [US-02 plan selection](US-02-plan-selection.md).

## Wireframes

| View | Review frames |
| --- | --- |
| Editable Summary | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-summary-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-summary-mobile.svg) |
| Terms and payment states | [In-place variants on the compact lane](wireframes/US-03-terms-and-payment-states.svg) |
| Confirmation, including reload | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-mobile.svg) |

Each country uses the same layouts and control order. The examples use fictitious values, local currency formatting and sample terms. The app presents the active country's published terms and current field and plan labels.

## Editable Summary

- Reuse the app header, main landmark, route-entry heading focus and informational **Datos / Plan / Resumen** stepper. A review heading identifies the step. The selected country is visible in the terms heading and the plan's currency.
- Show **Titular y vehículo** as a definition list in configured order with a nearby **Editar datos** link to same-country Details. Use the projected masked document in visible and accessible text. The **Plan elegido** card shows the current plan and final price with **Cambiar plan** linking to same-country Plans. Use the approved formatter with explicit **COP** or **CLP**. Both links preserve state under the existing Details and Plans rules.
- Put **Términos y condiciones de {país}** next in reading order. Present the plain text inline with preserved paragraph breaks. The page scrolls as the text grows. The labeled, initially unchecked native consent checkbox follows the text. Its checked state reflects consent for the current quote and revision. Show **Acepta los términos para continuar.** beside the unavailable payment action while acceptance is outstanding.
- Use a native radio group with visible legend **Resultado del pago (solo demostración)** and the options **Aprobado** and **Rechazado**. Default to **Aprobado** on initial entry. Associate **No se realizará un cobro real.** with the group as help. **Simular pago** is the single Pay action for either outcome and every payment retry. Its eligibility follows ADR-005.
- At 64 rem and above, use the established centered 58 rem composition with Details and plan side by side, followed by a reading lane for terms, consent, outcome and Pay. Below 64 rem, stack the plan after Details using the same DOM order. At compact widths, retain 16–20 px side gutters and use a full-width Pay button. Use auto-height panels, wrapping labels and unbroken-value wrapping where needed. Keep the action in normal page flow.

Reuse the existing `app-wizard-progress` and status-panel pattern, Tailwind canvas/paper/context/ink/line tokens, existing input and focus utilities, and the approved success, error and disabled treatments. Section titles, price emphasis and the quote number follow the approved type scale. Keep 44 px link and control targets and the 48 px primary action. [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md), [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Terms and payment states

| State | Visible response and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Reading terms on entry or retry | Keep the review and price visible. In the terms region show **Cargando términos…** until usable content is ready. Consent is unavailable and Pay stays disabled. |
| Terms unavailable | For empty, invalid or failed reads, including the Pay refresh, show **No pudimos cargar los términos.** with **Reintentar carga** in the terms region. Keep Details and plan. Pay stays blocked. If a successful recovery returns the same terms revision, text and quote snapshot, previously accepted consent can remain checked. Recovery returns to the review without starting payment. |
| Checking terms on Pay | Keep the review visible and reserve the single Pay action. Show **Comprobando los términos…** and disable repeat activation. The simulator begins only after the fresh read confirms the accepted terms and quote. |
| Terms changed on Pay | Replace the terms with the new text, clear consent, and show **Los términos cambiaron. Léelos y acéptalos para continuar.** before the updated text. A new acceptance followed by another **Simular pago** is required. |
| Processing | Keep the review, plan, terms and consent visible. Show **Procesando el pago simulado…** and keep Pay locked until settlement. An interrupted reload returns to the editable review if its prerequisites pass. Fresh consent is required before retry. |
| Rejected | Show **Pago simulado rechazado.** by the payment controls with **Tu cotización se conservó. Elige un resultado y vuelve a simular el pago.** The chosen **Rechazado** option remains visible. The user can select **Aprobado** or retry the chosen outcome using the same action. Retain Details, plan and still-current consent. |
| Approved | Replace all editable content with a terminal receipt. Show **Pago simulado aprobado**, **No se realizó un cobro.**, the country and a selectable **Número de cotización**. Keep the existing product header and completed stepper. On reload or return to the same completed quote, show the same reference even if published content changed. |
| Details or plan prerequisite missing | Reuse the existing redirect and recovery patterns for the earliest incomplete same-country step. Editable Summary is available after successful revalidation. |

## Keyboard, focus and announcements

- Use contextual anchor text for edits, an associated native checkbox label, and a native `fieldset` and `legend` for the radios. Keyboard order follows the review, terms, checkbox, radio group and Pay. Use standard Tab, Space, Enter and arrow-key behavior. Keep the disabled reason or status visible beside Pay. Preserve visible focus and the native outline in forced colors. [WAI grouping controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
- Announce loading, fresh checks and processing through a stable polite status region. Announce actionable failures once, using the existing accessible feedback pattern. Keep focus where it is while async work runs, with the focused Pay control retained as a target during the busy state. Convey the disabled state programmatically and suppress both keyboard and pointer activation while it remains focusable. If changed terms interrupt an active Pay interaction, move focus to the updated terms heading so it precedes the new text and checkbox. On terms failure, use the recovery control as the focus destination if the initiating target disappeared or became unavailable. A failed recovery with a stable Retry control keeps focus there. A successful recovery that removes the Retry control returns focus to the terms heading. A user who moved to an edit link while waiting keeps their focus.
- On rejection, announce the result while keeping focus in place if its target is still present. The user can reach the outcome choices from Pay with Shift+Tab. On first confirmation or a restored receipt, focus its heading and expose the reference as nearby selectable text. The heading and receipt content communicate success without relying on icon or color. Use a static busy cue under reduced motion. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

## Design verification map

| Approved criteria | Checks for implementation and QA |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US03-01, 02, 04 and 08 | Check both country projections, masked visible and spoken document values, option labels, currency, edit links and prerequisite recovery. |
| AC-US03-03 and 09 | Check long published terms at narrow widths, missing/invalid content, fresh Pay checks, a changed revision with renewed acceptance, and terms retry with focus and draft retention. |
| AC-US03-05, 06 and 07 | Exercise both outcome choices in each country, locked activation through both busy phases, rejection-to-approval retry, interrupted reload and same-number terminal receipt restoration. |
| AC-US03-10 | Check keyboard order, visible and unobscured focus, announcements, target sizes, reduced motion, forced colors and reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom. |

The wireframes and interaction guidance are pending human design approval.
"}

name: code-review-and-quality
description: Conducts multi-axis code review. Use before merging any change. Use when reviewing code written by yourself, another agent, or a human. Use when you need to assess code quality across multiple dimensions before it enters the main branch. Use when asked to review a diff or a pull request, even when the diff is pasted inline and the review looks quick to do from reading it.

# Code Review and Quality

## Overview

Multi-dimensional code review with quality gates. Every change gets reviewed before merge — no exceptions. Review covers five axes: correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance.

**The approval standard:** Approve a change when it definitely improves overall code health, even if it isn't perfect. Perfect code doesn't exist — the goal is continuous improvement. Don't block a change because it isn't exactly how you would have written it. If it improves the codebase and follows the project's conventions, approve it.

## When to Use

- Before merging any PR or change
- After completing a feature implementation
- When another agent or model produced code you need to evaluate
- When refactoring existing code
- After any bug fix (review both the fix and the regression test)

## The Five-Axis Review

Every review evaluates code across these dimensions:

### 1. Correctness

Does the code do what it claims to do?

- Does it match the spec or task requirements?
- Are edge cases handled (null, empty, boundary values)?
- Are error paths handled (not just the happy path)?
- Does it pass all tests? Are the tests actually testing the right things?
- Are there off-by-one errors, race conditions, or state inconsistencies?

### 2. Readability & Simplicity

Can another engineer (or agent) understand this code without the author explaining it?

- Are names descriptive and consistent with project conventions? (No `temp`, `data`, `result` without context)
- Is the control flow straightforward (avoid nested ternaries, deep callbacks)?
- Is the code organized logically (related code grouped, clear module boundaries)?
- Are there any "clever" tricks that should be simplified?
- **Could this be done in fewer lines?** (1000 lines where 100 suffice is a failure)
- **Are abstractions earning their complexity?** (Don't generalize until the third use case)
- Would comments help clarify non-obvious intent? (But don't comment obvious code.)
- Are there dead code artifacts: no-op variables (`_unused`), backwards-compat shims, or `// removed` comments?
- **Is a new conditional bolted onto an unrelated flow?** That's a design smell, not a nit — push the logic into its own helper, state, or policy instead of tangling an existing path.
- **Do repeated conditionals on the same shape appear?** They signal a missing model or dispatcher. A "temporary" branch is usually permanent debt.

### 3. Architecture

Does the change fit the system's design?

- Does it follow existing patterns or introduce a new one? If new, is it justified?
- Does it maintain clean module boundaries?
- Is there code duplication that should be shared?
- Are dependencies flowing in the right direction (no circular dependencies)?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over-engineered, not too coupled)?
- **Does this refactor reduce complexity or just relocate it?** Count the concepts a reader must hold to follow the change. If a "cleaner" version leaves that count unchanged, it isn't cleaner — prefer the restructuring that makes whole branches, modes, or layers disappear over one that re-centralizes the same logic. Prefer deleting an abstraction to polishing it.
- **Is feature-specific logic leaking into a shared or general-purpose module?** Keep logic in its owning layer, reuse the existing canonical helper instead of a near-duplicate, and don't normalize architectural drift.
- **Are type boundaries explicit?** Question gratuitous `any`/`unknown`/optional/casts and silent fallbacks that paper over an unclear invariant — making the boundary explicit often makes the surrounding control flow simpler.

### 4. Security

For detailed security guidance, see `security-and-hardening`. Does the change introduce vulnerabilities?

- Is user input validated and sanitized?
- Are secrets kept out of code, logs, and version control?
- Is authentication/authorization checked where needed?
- Are SQL queries parameterized (no string concatenation)?
- Are outputs encoded to prevent XSS?
- Are dependencies from trusted sources with no known vulnerabilities?
- Is data from external sources (APIs, logs, user content, config files) treated as untrusted?
- Are external data flows validated at system boundaries before use in logic or rendering?

### 5. Performance

For detailed profiling and optimization, see `performance-optimization`. Does the change introduce performance problems?

- Any N+1 query patterns?
- Any unbounded loops or unconstrained data fetching?
- Any synchronous operations that should be async?
- Any unnecessary re-renders in UI components?
- Any missing pagination on list endpoints?
- Any large objects created in hot paths?

## Structural Remedies

When you flag a structural problem, propose the move — not just the problem. A review that only says "this is complex" leaves the author guessing. Reach for a named restructuring:

- **Replace a chain of conditionals** with a typed model or an explicit dispatcher.
- **Collapse duplicate branches** into a single clearer flow.
- **Separate orchestration from business logic** so each reads on its own.
- **Move feature-specific logic** out of a shared module into the package that owns the concept.
- **Reuse the canonical helper** instead of a bespoke near-duplicate.
- **Make a type boundary explicit** so downstream branching disappears.
- **Delete a pass-through wrapper** that adds indirection without clarifying the API.
- **Extract a helper, or split a large file** into focused modules.

Prefer the remedy that removes moving pieces over one that spreads the same complexity around.

## Change Sizing

Small, focused changes are easier to review, faster to merge, and safer to deploy. Target these sizes:

```
~100 lines changed   → Good. Reviewable in one sitting.
~300 lines changed   → Acceptable if it's a single logical change.
~1000 lines changed  → Too large. Split it.
```

**Watch file size, not just diff size.** A small diff can still push a file past a healthy boundary — around 1000 *total* lines in a single file (distinct from the ~1000 *changed*-lines threshold above) is a common inspection signal, not a hard cap. When a change materially grows an already-large file, ask whether to extract helpers, subcomponents, or modules *first*, before piling more on. Decompose, then add.

**What counts as "one change":** A single self-contained modification that addresses one thing, includes related tests, and keeps the system functional after submission. One part of a feature — not the whole feature.

**Splitting strategies when a change is too large:**

| Strategy | How | When |
|----------|-----|------|
| **Stack** | Submit a small change, start the next one based on it | Sequential dependencies |
| **By file group** | Separate changes for groups needing different reviewers | Cross-cutting concerns |
| **Horizontal** | Create shared code/stubs first, then consumers | Layered architecture |
| **Vertical** | Break into smaller full-stack slices of the feature | Feature work |

**When large changes are acceptable:** Complete file deletions and automated refactoring where the reviewer only needs to verify intent, not every line.

**Separate refactoring from feature work.** A change that refactors existing code and adds new behavior is two changes — submit them separately. Small cleanups (variable renaming) can be included at reviewer discretion.

## Change Descriptions

Every change needs a description that stands alone in version control history.

**First line:** Short, imperative, standalone. "Delete the FizzBuzz RPC" not "Deleting the FizzBuzz RPC." Must be informative enough that someone searching history can understand the change without reading the diff.

**Body:** What is changing and why. Include context, decisions, and reasoning not visible in the code itself. Link to bug numbers, benchmark results, or design docs where relevant. Acknowledge approach shortcomings when they exist.

**Anti-patterns:** "Fix bug," "Fix build," "Add patch," "Moving code from A to B," "Phase 1," "Add convenience functions."

## Review Process

### Step 1: Understand the Context

Before looking at code, understand the intent:

```
- What is this change trying to accomplish?
- What spec or task does it implement?
- What is the expected behavior change?
```

### Step 2: Review the Tests First

Tests reveal intent and coverage:

```
- Do tests exist for the change?
- Do they test behavior (not implementation details)?
- Are edge cases covered?
- Do tests have descriptive names?
- Would the tests catch a regression if the code changed?
```

Answer the last question by experiment, not by reading. Invert one condition the change adds (drop a negation, swap `&&` for `||`), run the suite, then restore the file from a copy. A mutation that stays green is a finding: name the test case that is missing. For a project-wide mutation score, see `constraint-driven-development`.

### Step 3: Review the Implementation

Walk through the code with the five axes in mind:

```
For each file changed:
1. Correctness: Does this code do what the test says it should?
2. Readability: Can I understand this without help?
3. Architecture: Does this fit the system?
4. Security: Any vulnerabilities?
5. Performance: Any bottlenecks?
```

### Step 4: Categorize Findings

Before reporting a finding, check it against the callers, guards and tests that reach the changed code, and drop it if they rule it out. Label defects that already exist in the base separately from regressions this change introduces. Zero findings is a valid result; do not invent one.

Label every comment with its severity so the author knows what's required vs optional:

| Prefix | Meaning | Author Action |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| *(no prefix)* | Required change | Must address before merge |
| **Critical:** | Blocks merge | Security vulnerability, data loss, broken functionality |
| **Nit:** | Minor, optional | Author may ignore — formatting, style preferences |
| **Optional:** / **Consider:** | Suggestion | Worth considering but not required |
| **FYI** | Informational only | No action needed — context for future reference |

This prevents authors from treating all feedback as mandatory and wasting time on optional suggestions.

**Lead with what matters.** Order findings by leverage: correctness and security first, then structural regressions and missed simplifications, then everything else. Don't bury a real issue under cosmetic nits — a few high-conviction comments beat a long list. If you have one structural problem and ten nits, the structural problem *is* the review.

### Step 5: Verify the Verification

Check the author's verification story:

```
- What tests were run?
- Did the build pass?
- Was the change tested manually?
- Are there screenshots for UI changes?
- Is there a before/after comparison?
```

Before you run tests or probes yourself, confirm the checkout is clean and on the reviewed ref (`git status --short` is empty and `git rev-parse HEAD` matches the PR head), and name that ref in the review. A working copy can hold uncommitted edits from another session, so evidence from it may describe code that is not in the change.

## Multi-Model Review Pattern

Use different models for different review perspectives:

```
Model A writes the code
    │
    ▼
Model B reviews for correctness and architecture
    │
    ▼
Model A addresses the feedback
    │
    ▼
Human makes the final call
```

This catches issues that a single model might miss — different models have different blind spots.

**Example prompt for a review agent:**
```
Review this code change for correctness, security, and adherence to
our project conventions. The spec says [X]. The change should [Y].
Flag any issues as Critical, Required, Optional, or Nit.
```

## Dead Code Hygiene

After any refactoring or implementation change, check for orphaned code:

1. Identify code that is now unreachable or unused
2. List it explicitly
3. **Ask before deleting:** "Should I remove these now-unused elements: [list]?"

Don't leave dead code lying around — it confuses future readers and agents. But don't silently delete things you're not sure about. When in doubt, ask.

```
DEAD CODE IDENTIFIED:
- formatLegacyDate() in src/utils/date.ts — replaced by formatDate()
- OldTaskCard component in src/components/ — replaced by TaskCard
- LEGACY_API_URL constant in src/config.ts — no remaining references
→ Safe to remove these?
```

## Review Speed

Slow reviews block entire teams. The cost of context-switching to review is less than the waiting cost imposed on others.

- **Respond within one business day** — this is the maximum, not the target
- **Ideal cadence:** Respond shortly after a review request arrives, unless deep in focused coding. A typical change should complete multiple review rounds in a single day
- **Prioritize fast individual responses** over quick final approval. Quick feedback reduces frustration even if multiple rounds are needed
- **Large changes:** Ask the author to split them rather than reviewing one massive changeset

## Handling Disagreements

When resolving review disputes, apply this hierarchy:

1. **Technical facts and data** override opinions and preferences
2. **Style guides** are the absolute authority on style matters
3. **Software design** must be evaluated on engineering principles, not personal preference
4. **Codebase consistency** is acceptable if it doesn't degrade overall health

**Don't accept "I'll clean it up later."** Experience shows deferred cleanup rarely happens. Require cleanup before submission unless it's a genuine emergency. If surrounding issues can't be addressed in this change, require filing a bug with self-assignment.

## Honesty in Review

When reviewing code — whether written by you, another agent, or a human:

- **Don't rubber-stamp.** "LGTM" without evidence of review helps no one.
- **Don't soften real issues.** "This might be a minor concern" when it's a bug that will hit production is dishonest.
- **Quantify problems when possible.** "This N+1 query will add ~50ms per item in the list" is better than "this could be slow."
- **Push back on approaches with clear problems.** Sycophancy is a failure mode in reviews. If the implementation has issues, say so directly and propose alternatives.
- **Accept override gracefully.** If the author has full context and disagrees, defer to their judgment. Comment on code, not people — reframe personal critiques to focus on the code itself.

## Dependency Discipline

Part of code review is dependency review:

**Before adding any dependency:**
1. Does the existing stack solve this? (Often it does.)
2. How large is the dependency? (Check bundle impact.)
3. Is it actively maintained? (Check last commit, open issues.)
4. Does it have known vulnerabilities? (`npm audit`)
5. What's the license? (Must be compatible with the project.)

**Rule:** Prefer standard library and existing utilities over new dependencies. Every dependency is a liability.

**Upgrading an existing dependency** is a code change like any other, and the riskiest upgrades are the ones merged in bulk with a message like "bump deps." Review them with the same discipline:

1. **Read the changelog, not just the version number.** Semver is a promise the maintainer may not have kept — a "patch" can carry a behavioral change. For a major bump, read the migration notes and find what breaks.
2. **One dependency per change.** Upgrade and merge them individually (or in small related groups). When a bulk bump breaks the build, you've lost which package did it; a single-package change makes the cause obvious and the revert clean.
3. **Let the tests decide.** The upgrade is verified by a green suite before *and* after, not by "it installed." If coverage around the dependency's behavior is thin, that gap is the real finding — add a test first.
4. **Mind the transitive graph.** Most installed packages are ones nobody chose directly. Review the lockfile diff, not just `package.json`; a single direct bump can pull in dozens of indirect changes.
5. **Keep the lockfile honest.** Commit it, review its diff, and never hand-edit it. The lockfile is the thing that actually pins what ships.

For triaging `npm audit` findings and supply-chain risk (typosquatting, compromised maintainers), follow the `security-and-hardening` skill — this section covers the upgrade *workflow*, that one covers the security verdict.

## The Review Checklist

```markdown
## Review: [PR/Change title]

### Context
- [ ] I understand what this change does and why

### Correctness
- [ ] Change matches spec/task requirements
- [ ] Edge cases handled
- [ ] Error paths handled
- [ ] Tests cover the change adequately

### Readability
- [ ] Names are clear and consistent
- [ ] Logic is straightforward
- [ ] No unnecessary complexity

### Architecture
- [ ] Follows existing patterns
- [ ] No unnecessary coupling or dependencies
- [ ] Appropriate abstraction level
- [ ] Refactors reduce complexity rather than relocate it
- [ ] No feature logic in shared modules; file stays within a healthy size

### Security
- [ ] No secrets in code
- [ ] Input validated at boundaries
- [ ] No injection vulnerabilities
- [ ] Auth checks in place
- [ ] External data sources treated as untrusted

### Performance
- [ ] No N+1 patterns
- [ ] No unbounded operations
- [ ] Pagination on list endpoints

### Verification
- [ ] Tests pass
- [ ] Build succeeds
- [ ] Manual verification done (if applicable)

### Verdict
- [ ] **Approve** — Ready to merge
- [ ] **Request changes** — Issues must be addressed
```
## See Also

- For detailed security review guidance, see `../../references/security-checklist.md`
- For performance review checks, see `../../references/performance-checklist.md`

## Common Rationalizations

| Rationalization | Reality |
|---|---|
| "It works, that's good enough" | Working code that's unreadable, insecure, or architecturally wrong creates debt that compounds. |
| "I wrote it, so I know it's correct" | Authors are blind to their own assumptions. Every change benefits from another set of eyes. |
| "We'll clean it up later" | Later never comes. The review is the quality gate — use it. Require cleanup before merge, not after. |
| "AI-generated code is probably fine" | AI code needs more scrutiny, not less. It's confident and plausible, even when wrong. |
| "The tests pass, so it's good" | Tests are necessary but not sufficient. They don't catch architecture problems, security issues, or readability concerns. |
| "The refactor makes it cleaner" | Relocating complexity isn't reducing it. If the reader still holds the same number of concepts, the structure didn't improve — look for the version where branches disappear. |
| "It's only a small addition to this file" | Small diffs still push files past a healthy size and bolt branches onto unrelated flows. Judge the resulting structure, not the diff size. |
| "It's just a version bump" | A bump is a behavior change you didn't write. Read the changelog; semver doesn't guarantee no breakage. |
| "I'll upgrade everything in one PR to save time" | A bulk bump that breaks the build hides which package did it. One dependency per change keeps the cause and the revert clean. |

## Red Flags

- PRs merged without any review
- Review that only checks if tests pass (ignoring other axes)
- "LGTM" without evidence of actual review
- Security-sensitive changes without security-focused review
- Large PRs that are "too big to review properly" (split them)
- No regression tests with bug fix PRs
- Review comments without severity labels — makes it unclear what's required vs optional
- Accepting "I'll fix it later" — it never happens
- A refactor that moves code around without reducing the number of concepts a reader must hold
- A change that grows an already-large file instead of decomposing it
- New conditionals scattered into unrelated code paths (a missing abstraction)
- A bespoke helper that duplicates an existing canonical one, or feature logic placed in a shared module
- A bulk "bump dependencies" PR with no changelog review and no per-package isolation
- A lockfile change that's hand-edited, uncommitted, or merged without reviewing its diff

## Verification

After review is complete:

- [ ] All Critical issues are resolved
- [ ] All Required (no-prefix) changes are resolved or explicitly deferred with justification
- [ ] Tests pass
- [ ] Build succeeds
- [ ] The verification story is documented (what changed, how it was verified)
- [ ] Dependency upgrades were reviewed against their changelog, isolated per package, and verified by a green suite with the lockfile diff reviewed

**Presumptive blockers:** surface and propose the simpler design for each of these; escalate to Required only when the change actively makes structure worse: a refactor that relocates complexity instead of reducing it; a change that pushes a file past the size boundary with no decomposition; feature logic added to a shared module; a near-duplicate of an existing canonical helper; a silent fallback that hides an unclear invariant.
# Global Agent Instructions — Multi-Country Car Insurance

## Purpose and language
Build a multi-country car insurance quoting app for Colombia (CO) and Chile (CL) using Angular 21+ and Strapi 5+. Make the AI-assisted development process explicit, reproducible, reviewable, and traceable.
**All project-owned content must be written in English**: prompts, agent instructions, commit messages, specs, ADRs, code comments, tests, documentation, and review reports. User-facing insurance copy may be Spanish because it is country-specific business content supplied by Strapi. The original technical assessment remains unchanged.

## Sources of truth
- Read `requirements/technical-assessment.pdf` before interpreting a user story.
- Preserve the original story IDs: US-01, US-02, US-03.
- Write `spec/US-XX.md` before implementing a story. A human must explicitly approve its content.
- Record unresolved ambiguities as questions or assumptions, not as requirements from the assessment.
- Architecture decisions must be recorded in `docs/adr/`, including at least the country differentiation strategy.

## Technical constraints
- Angular 21+ with standalone components, signals, built-in `@if` and `@for`, and no NgModules.
- Strapi 5+ for business-managed content.
- One Angular app and one build serve Colombia and Chile.
- Configure country-specific fields, order, options, validations, plans, coverage, terms, and copy in Strapi without an Angular redeployment.
- Build dynamic forms with typed configuration models and explicit runtime validation.
- Never expose a Strapi write-privileged token in the browser; keep public read permissions minimal and document them.
- Use only fictitious data. Do not integrate a payment provider or real card details.
- Preserve wizard state in the frontend. Prevent duplicate simulated payments.
- Support keyboard navigation, accessible labels, responsive layout, and clear loading/empty/error states.

# Code Review and Quality

## Overview

Multi-dimensional code review with quality gates. Every change gets reviewed before merge — no exceptions. Review covers five axes: correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance.

**The approval standard:** Approve a change when it definitely improves overall code health, even if it isn't perfect. Perfect code doesn't exist — the goal is continuous improvement. Don't block a change because it isn't exactly how you would have written it. If it improves the codebase and follows the project's conventions, approve it.

## When to Use

- Before merging any PR or change
- After completing a feature implementation
- When another agent or model produced code you need to evaluate
- When refactoring existing code
- After any bug fix (review both the fix and the regression test)

## The Five-Axis Review

Every review evaluates code across these dimensions:

### 1. Correctness

Does the code do what it claims to do?

- Does it match the spec or task requirements?
- Are edge cases handled (null, empty, boundary values)?
- Are error paths handled (not just the happy path)?
- Does it pass all tests? Are the tests actually testing the right things?
- Are there off-by-one errors, race conditions, or state inconsistencies?

### 2. Readability & Simplicity

Can another engineer (or agent) understand this code without the author explaining it?

- Are names descriptive and consistent with project conventions? (No `temp`, `data`, `result` without context)
- Is the control flow straightforward (avoid nested ternaries, deep callbacks)?
- Is the code organized logically (related code grouped, clear module boundaries)?
- Are there any "clever" tricks that should be simplified?
- **Could this be done in fewer lines?** (1000 lines where 100 suffice is a failure)
- **Are abstractions earning their complexity?** (Don't generalize until the third use case)
- Would comments help clarify non-obvious intent? (But don't comment obvious code.)
- Are there dead code artifacts: no-op variables (`_unused`), backwards-compat shims, or `// removed` comments?
- **Is a new conditional bolted onto an unrelated flow?** That's a design smell, not a nit — push the logic into its own helper, state, or policy instead of tangling an existing path.
- **Do repeated conditionals on the same shape appear?** They signal a missing model or dispatcher. A "temporary" branch is usually permanent debt.

### 3. Architecture

Does the change fit the system's design?

- Does it follow existing patterns or introduce a new one? If new, is it justified?
- Does it maintain clean module boundaries?
- Is there code duplication that should be shared?
- Are dependencies flowing in the right direction (no circular dependencies)?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over-engineered, not too coupled)?
- **Does this refactor reduce complexity or just relocate it?** Count the concepts a reader must hold to follow the change. If a "cleaner" version leaves that count unchanged, it isn't cleaner — prefer the restructuring that makes whole branches, modes, or layers disappear over one that re-centralizes the same logic. Prefer deleting an abstraction to polishing it.
- **Is feature-specific logic leaking into a shared or general-purpose module?** Keep logic in its owning layer, reuse the existing canonical helper instead of a near-duplicate, and don't normalize architectural drift.
- **Are type boundaries explicit?** Question gratuitous `any`/`unknown`/optional/casts and silent fallbacks that paper over an unclear invariant — making the boundary explicit often makes the surrounding control flow simpler.

### 4. Security

For detailed security guidance, see `security-and-hardening`. Does the change introduce vulnerabilities?

- Is user input validated and sanitized?
- Are secrets kept out of code, logs, and version control?
- Is authentication/authorization checked where needed?
- Are SQL queries parameterized (no string concatenation)?
- Are outputs encoded to prevent XSS?
- Are dependencies from trusted sources with no known vulnerabilities?
- Is data from external sources (APIs, logs, user content, config files) treated as untrusted?
- Are external data flows validated at system boundaries before use in logic or rendering?

### 5. Performance

For detailed profiling and optimization, see `performance-optimization`. Does the change introduce performance problems?

- Any N+1 query patterns?
- Any unbounded loops or unconstrained data fetching?
- Any synchronous operations that should be async?
- Any unnecessary re-renders in UI components?
- Any missing pagination on list endpoints?
- Any large objects created in hot paths?

## Structural Remedies

When you flag a structural problem, propose the move — not just the problem. A review that only says "this is complex" leaves the author guessing. Reach for a named restructuring:

- **Replace a chain of conditionals** with a typed model or an explicit dispatcher.
- **Collapse duplicate branches** into a single clearer flow.
- **Separate orchestration from business logic** so each reads on its own.
- **Move feature-specific logic** out of a shared module into the package that owns the concept.
- **Reuse the canonical helper** instead of a bespoke near-duplicate.
- **Make a type boundary explicit** so downstream branching disappears.
- **Delete a pass-through wrapper** that adds indirection without clarifying the API.
- **Extract a helper, or split a large file** into focused modules.

Prefer the remedy that removes moving pieces over one that spreads the same complexity around.

## Change Sizing

Small, focused changes are easier to review, faster to merge, and safer to deploy. Target these sizes:

```
~100 lines changed   → Good. Reviewable in one sitting.
~300 lines changed   → Acceptable if it's a single logical change.
~1000 lines changed  → Too large. Split it.
```

**Watch file size, not just diff size.** A small diff can still push a file past a healthy boundary — around 1000 *total* lines in a single file (distinct from the ~1000 *changed*-lines threshold above) is a common inspection signal, not a hard cap. **Story:** US-03 — Summary and payment  
**Specification:** [US-03 Draft 2](../../spec/US-03.md)  
**Architecture:** [ADR-005](../../docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), with ADR-001 through ADR-004 reused  
**Design:** [Approved US-03 design](../../docs/design/US-03-summary-and-payment.md)  
**QA agent:** `/root/us03_qa`, configured QA role, `gpt-6-luna` / `xhigh`  
**Skills used:** `test-driven-development`, `angular-developer`  
**Native session ID:** Not available in this execution. The original activity remains in the Codex collaboration session.

## Verification scope and environment

Independent QA covered the active-country Summary projection, document masking, selected plan and final price, country terms and consent, terms refresh, both deterministic payment outcomes, duplicate activation, retry, route prerequisites, interrupted reload and completed receipt restoration. The complete browser quote flow ran in Colombia and Chile.

The QA app used Chrome against Angular on `127.0.0.1:4200`, proxied to Strapi 5.63 on `127.0.0.1:1338`. Strapi used the disposable database `/private/tmp/us03-qa-run/strapi.sqlite`. No existing development volume or customer data was used. Local server binding and Chrome launch required scoped sandbox escalation because the sandbox denied loopback binding and browser process launch.

## Acceptance criteria

| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-US03-01 — Current quote summary | T-US03-01, country browser cases, exact configured owner and vehicle fields, selected Esencial plan, COP/CLP final price, and country isolation. | Pass |
| AC-US03-02 — Shared document masking | T-US03-02, browser-visible masked long document for both countries and no raw value in the page. `quote-review.spec.ts` also covers long, short, one-character and separator cases. | Pass |
| AC-US03-03 — Country terms and consent | T-US03-03, T-US03-11, both country flows and the isolated Strapi publication test. Checks the terms envelope and revision digest, no-store, country-specific bodies, consent, changed terms, and fresh review before payment. | Pass |
| AC-US03-04 — Edit and change plan | T-US03-04, both country flows return to Details and Plans after rejection, preserve the entered owner and selected plan, then return to Summary. | Pass |
| AC-US03-05 — Successful simulated payment | T-US03-05, both country flows check Approved default, one attempt despite repeated keyboard activation, payment status announcements, one receipt, and no payment action after completion. | Pass |

| AC-US03-07 — Reload and completed receipt | T-US03-07, interrupted terms check reload returns to editable Summary with consent cleared; both main flows reload the same completed quote number. | Pass |
| AC-US03-08 — Details and plan prerequisites | T-US03-08 direct Summary routes for both countries redirect to Details. The existing US-02 direct-route case also passed in the broader run when it reached the test. | Pass |
| AC-US03-09 — Recoverable terms failure | T-US03-09, T-US03-11, Colombia recovers from an unavailable first read; Chile receives a changed revision before Pay and requires new consent. Strapi integration covers changed, draft, invalid and unpublished content. | Pass |
| AC-US03-10 — Keyboard and responsive use | T-US03-10, plan selection, consent and both payment outcomes use keyboard input; checking and processing are announced. Desktop runs at 1280 px and Chile mobile at 320 px with no horizontal overflow. | Pass |

## Finding

### US03-QA-01 — Medium, blocking full-suite QA handoff · Resolved

- **Affected artifact:** `e2e/us02-qa.spec.ts:146`
- **Related criterion:** US-02 handoff regression check; US-03 AC-US03-01
- **Finding:** The earlier US-02 Colombia handoff case expected the former Summary placeholder heading `Resumen`. US-03 now renders the approved Summary heading `Revisa tu cotización`.
- **Correction:** The Developer updated the handoff test to verify the Summary heading, selected Ruta plan and same-country plan-change link.
- **Resolution evidence:** The full 22-case Playwright suite passed against the isolated static Compose app. This finding required no production behavior change.
- **History:** The first full run against Angular `ng serve` had 19/22 pass. Two other API 404 assertions received the dev server's SPA fallback. The static-host rerun confirmed both expected 404s and resolved this finding.

## Environment limitations and run history

The initial broad browser run used Angular `ng serve`, which returned its SPA fallback for two unmatched `/api/form-configurations` and `/api/plans` requests that the existing tests expect to return 404. The full suite then passed 22/22 against the isolated static Compose deployment, which confirmed the production-style API responses. The dedicated US-03 terms API boundary test also passed against Strapi for its generated-route, query and method cases.

An initial QA test draft had two incorrect assertions: it expected Colombia terms before the deliberately simulated failed read was retried and assumed document masking removed punctuation. Both assertions were corrected. An initial broad-suite invocation after the isolated dev servers had been stopped returned connection-refused errors. The servers were restarted for the dev-server run, then the complete static Compose run passed. These test and environment issues were not application defects.

Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks were not run. The browser verification covers keyboard operation, accessible names, live status text, and 320 px reflow. No automated axe scan was run.

## QA recommendation

The US-03 behavior passed dedicated browser, CMS integration, unit and full cross-story browser coverage. US03-QA-01 is resolved with evidence. No blocking implementation defect was reproduced. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks remain unverified.

If the owner approves preserving an existing Colombia Ruta price, add `--preserve-co-ruta-price PRICE` to both preview and apply. Use COP major units with two decimal places and no grouping separators. For example, use `--preserve-co-ruta-price 179900.00` for COP 179.900,00. Both stored versions must already have exactly that price. The sync preserves it and still checks every other field against the fixtures.

## Configuration and data boundaries

- The public app uses same-origin GET paths under `/api/quote-content/v1/:country/` for `form`, `plans`, and `terms`. The Strapi Public role has only `readForm`, `readPlans`, and `readTerms` under `api::quote-content.quote-content`. The static host proxies these three reads. The public frontend uses no API token.
- Never add duplicate field keys, option keys or semantic purposes. Field order is numeric, then stable field key on ties. Date of birth with the 18-year rule and vehicle year with its range rule are required for a usable form.
- Enter a rule argument or field default in the Strapi JSON editor as an object with a single `value` property, for example `{"value": 18}`, `{"value": false}` or `{"value": "2020-01-01"}`. Leave it empty for argument-free rules or fields with no default. Required selects start unselected and cannot have defaults. Present but invalid content leaves the whole form unavailable with a retry action.
- The version 1 decoder accepts up to 40 fields, 60 options per select, 12 rules per field and 240 UTF-16 units per content string. Text values allow up to 256 Unicode code points. Patterns are whole-value checks limited to 120 pattern units, literal characters, character classes and bounded counts through 24. The matcher uses a bounded set of offsets.
- Each country catalog may include up to 40 active published plans with up to 20 entries per coverage or benefit list. Plans sort by numeric order, then stable document ID. A malformed active published plan makes the country's catalog unavailable until the content is corrected.
- Each country has one published Terms document with a nonblank body of up to 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Missing, duplicate or invalid published terms block payment until recovered.
- Drafts and plan choices are isolated by URL country and retained in the current tab's `sessionStorage`, with a memory fallback if storage is unavailable. Reload revalidates against fresh published configuration. Quote data is excluded from API payloads, shareable URLs, and server persistence. SQLite holds Strapi content and its administrative metadata.
- Frontend SVGs are individual assets from Tabler Icons v3.41.1, tinted for the approved design. The Strapi favicon derives from the same shield. See the [MIT license](frontend/public/icons/TABLER-LICENSE.txt).

## Verify

Use Node 24 and the pinned pnpm 11 version in `package.json` for local tooling.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test
pnpm lint
pnpm build
pnpm test:content
```

The content test starts an isolated local Strapi fixture and verifies that published revisions are served while drafts stay private.

With the Compose app listening on port 8080, install Playwright's Chromium browser once and run browser tests.

```sh
pnpm exec playwright install chromium
pnpm test:e2e
```

For an optional local development workflow without Compose, first run `pnpm --filter @quote/contract build`. In the `backend/` directory, run `HOST=127.0.0.1 STRAPI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true node scripts/start.mjs develop`. In the `frontend/` directory, run `pnpm start --proxy-config proxy.conf.json`. The dev server uses the same public routes at port 4200. Set `QUOTE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4200` to target it with Playwright.

## Requirements and project evidence

- [US-01 specification](spec/US-01.md), [US-02 specification](spec/US-02.md), and [US-03 specification](spec/US-03.md) define the approved behavior and acceptance-test identifiers. [ADR-004](docs/adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) and the [US-02 design](docs/design/US-02-plan-selection.md) cover the catalog and plan selection.
- [Country strategy](docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [dynamic contract](docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), [frontend quote state](docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md), and [wireframes](docs/design/US-01-wireframes.md) record the approved decisions.
- [ADR-005](docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md) and the [US-03 design](docs/design/US-03-summary-and-payment.md) cover terms, consent, and simulated payment.
- [Workflow](FLOW.md), [agent model policy](docs/agent-model-policy.md), and [session evidence guidance](logs/README.md) describe the agent and approval process.
- The [US-02 QA report](reports/qa/US-02-qa-report.md) and [independent review](reviews/US-02-review.md) record the story verification results and remaining checks.

## Requirements pending for project delivery

Independent US-03 verification and final human approval are pending. Native screen-reader verification remains pending. Original agent activity is preserved in Codex. A safe, unedited repository export remains pending.

## Proposed decision

### Published terms contract

Create a Terms collection with Draft & Publish and one document per country. Use the existing country enum and a required, nonblank multiline plain-text body of at most 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Preserve the body as returned by Strapi, including paragraph breaks. Read only the published country document through the Document Service, selecting only country and body. Read up to two documents to detect duplicate publications and fail if either the country or body is invalid. Seed one fictitious, country-specific publication for Colombia and Chile in the existing startup workflow. Track seeding separately from Forms and Plans, skip countries with existing Terms documents during initial seeding, and preserve editorial changes and deliberate unpublication on subsequent starts. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status)

Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/terms` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing country parser and reject request query parameters. Project `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, revision, text }`. Define `revision` as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON tuple `[1, country, text]`, computed by Strapi from the projected values. It identifies the exact country text the user can accept. Publishing changed text changes its revision and republishing identical text keeps the revision. The shared `@quote/contract` decoder checks the envelope version, expected country, revision format and text bounds at the server and browser boundaries. Angular presents terms as text, preserving line breaks and treating markup as literal content. [Angular security](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)

| Outcome | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Valid published document | `200` with the terms envelope |
| Unexpected query parameters or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
| No published document | `404 TERMS_NOT_PUBLISHED` |
| Duplicate or invalid published configuration | `503 TERMS_UNAVAILABLE` |
| CMS retrieval failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |

Reuse the `{ error: { code } }` envelope and `Cache-Control: no-store` on handler outcomes. Extend the same-origin, GET-only proxy allowlist and add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readTerms` to the Public role alongside Form and Plans. Generated CRUD, draft and admin access, and write credentials stay outside the public contract. The terms request carries the country in the path and no quote, consent or payment data. The proxy bypasses caching as it does for Form and Plans. [HTTP caching](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html)

### Summary and consent

Extend the existing Summary handoff. Build a read-only review projection from the active country's validated, reconciled Details and freshly selected Plan. Use current field order, labels and option labels, the existing money formatter and the plan's final price. Mask the `identityDocument` value before it enters the review projection so both visible and accessible output use the same masked string. Apply Q-US03-01 to alphanumeric characters, preserving separators. Keep the raw value in the existing Details draft only. There is no additional form field or network contract for the review.

Read Terms on Summary entry and explicit retry through the existing `HttpClient` and signals pattern. Bind consent in memory to the active country, terms revision and the review snapshot. Compare snapshots by value using the current field identifiers, kinds and normalized values, and the selected plan ID and final money value. Navigation back to edit preserves Details and the plan candidate under their existing rules. A change to normalized quote data, plan, price or terms revision invalidates consent. Cancellation and generation checks prevent superseded responses from replacing active terms. Loading or failed reads leave the review available with payment blocked. A successful recovery read may restore eligibility using prior consent only if the revision, text and quote snapshot still match. Recovery itself never invokes the simulator. The next Pay still performs its own fresh read. [Angular HTTP requests](https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests)

### One simulated attempt and terminal recovery

1. The quote feature owns one attempt state per country. A single Pay command checks the live editable Summary prerequisites, consent and absence of a busy or completed payment. It synchronously reserves an attempt before requesting fresh country Terms. That reservation locks submission during both the refresh and the simulation. The attempt captures the country, active Summary generation, consent binding and the selected demo outcome.
2. Only the current attempt may act on the refresh result. Recheck the active country and Summary generation, current Details and plan validity, quote snapshot, and consent. ## Scope

Reviewed the US-03 implementation and tests against the approved story artifacts, including:

- `shared/src/terms.ts` and `shared/test/us03.test.ts`
- `backend/src/api/quote-content/content-types/terms/schema.json`
- `backend/src/api/quote-content/terms-projection.ts`
- `backend/src/api/quote-content/controllers/quote-content.ts`
- `backend/src/api/quote-content/routes/quote-content.ts`
- `backend/src/index.ts`, `backend/src/seed-terms.ts`, and `backend/test/public-content.test.mjs`
- `frontend/src/app/quote/quote-payment.ts`, `quote-review.ts`, `quote-summary.ts`, and `quote-summary.html`
- `frontend/src/app/quote/quote-state.ts`, `quote-page.ts`, `plan-list.ts`, and their relevant tests
- `frontend/src/styles.css` and `deploy/quote.conf`
- `e2e/us03-qa.spec.ts` and the corrected US-02 handoff assertion in `e2e/us02-qa.spec.ts`
- Relevant README, approved design, architecture and specification traceability

The review focused on country isolation, public permissions, terms validation and freshness, document masking, quote snapshot consent, duplicate payment attempts, late asynchronous responses, reload receipt recovery, accessible controls and test evidence.

## Verification evidence

Independent QA recorded:

- `CI=1 pnpm test`: 15 shared and 13 Angular tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter quote-cms test:content`: two Strapi integration tests passed.
- Dedicated US-03 Playwright suite: five tests passed.
- Full Playwright suite: 22 tests passed against a fresh isolated static Compose deployment.
- Lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed.

The QA environment used a disposable Strapi SQLite database and isolated Compose project. No existing content volume was used. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks remain unverified, as documented in the QA report.

## Findings

No blocking or non-blocking code findings.

### QA finding history

- **US03-QA-01 — Medium, resolved:** The existing US-02 browser handoff assertion expected the placeholder Summary heading. The Developer updated it to assert the implemented Summary heading, selected plan and same-country plan-change link. QA verified the correction in the full 22-test production-style Compose run.
- The QA report also records early test assertion and environment setup failures. They were corrected or avoided in the final runs and were not application findings.

## Review notes

- The terms endpoint selects published country documents only, limits the result to two to detect duplicates, projects only country and body, computes the revision from the displayed text and returns `no-store`. QA verified the Public role grants and request boundary.
- Terms are rendered through Angular interpolation. The decoder validates country, revision format, nonblank content and size before the response enters state.
- The payment command reserves the attempt synchronously by moving to `checking` before the terms refresh. Repeated activation is guarded by `canPay`, and the captured country, generation and quote snapshot are checked before processing and settlement. Navigation cancels the request/timer and invalidates late callbacks.
- The selected document is masked in the read-only review projection. The consent snapshot uses a per-country draft revision, field identifiers and kinds, selected plan ID and final price. The draft revision advances only when underlying normalized field values or kinds change, so edits to a hidden identity prefix invalidate consent even when the visible mask is unchanged.
- Receipts contain only a version, country and opaque random quote reference in bounded tab storage. Restore validates version, country and reference. The terminal receipt route bypasses editable Summary and prevents duplicate payment. Interrupted payment state and consent remain memory-only.

## Recommendation

**Approved.** The reviewed changes implement the approved US-03 specification, ADR-005 and design, and QA evidence covers both countries and the complete successful and rejected payment retry flows. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast verification remain unverified for the project-level delivery record.

- **Affected artifact:** `e2e/us02-qa.spec.ts:146`
- **Related criterion:** US-02 handoff regression check; US-03 AC-US03-01
- **Finding:** The earlier US-02 Colombia handoff case expected the former Summary placeholder heading `Resumen`. US-03 now renders the approved Summary heading `Revisa tu cotización`.
- **Correction:** The Developer updated the handoff test to verify the Summary heading, selected Ruta plan and same-country plan-change link.
- **Resolution evidence:** The full 22-case Playwright suite passed against the isolated static Compose app. This finding required no production behavior change.
- **History:** The first full run against Angular `ng serve` had 19/22 pass. Two other API 404 assertions received the dev server's SPA fallback. The static-host rerun confirmed both expected 404s and resolved this finding.

## Environment limitations and run history

The initial broad browser run used Angular `ng serve`, which returned its SPA fallback for two unmatched `/api/form-configurations` and `/api/plans` requests that the existing tests expect to return 404. The full suite then passed 22/22 against the isolated static Compose deployment, which confirmed the production-style API responses. The dedicated US-03 terms API boundary test also passed against Strapi for its generated-route, query and method cases.

An initial QA test draft had two incorrect assertions: it expected Colombia terms before the deliberately simulated failed read was retried and assumed document masking removed punctuation. Both assertions were corrected. An initial broad-suite invocation after the isolated dev servers had been stopped returned connection-refused errors. The servers were restarted for the dev-server run, then the complete static Compose run passed. These test and environment issues were not application defects.

Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks were not run. The browser verification covers keyboard operation, accessible names, live status text, and 320 px reflow. No automated axe scan was run.

## Approved copy revision re-verification, 2026-11-22

The QA flow now checks that the retired fictitious-data introduction and identity-number hint are absent from Details; Summary exposes the `Resultado de prueba` group and `Pagar` action without the former demonstration heading, no-real-charge sentence, or `Simular pago` action; and the approved receipt contains no country name or standalone no-charge sentence. These are copy acceptance checks, not a new QA defect. The Colombia and Chile full quote flows each exercised rejection, retry with preserved owner and selected plan, approval, and reload of the same receipt. Both passed on the refreshed local Compose app at `127.0.0.1:8080`. The isolated terms API, direct-route prerequisite, and interrupted-check reload tests also passed in the same five-test run.

During the first follow-up attempt, the new Details copy checks completed, but the CO flow timed out because the QA helper expected the former `Ejemplo Motor` option while the refreshed CO seed offers `Mazda` and `Chevrolet`. The test helper now selects the first configured brand option. This was test fixture drift, not an application defect. The focused rerun passed 2/2 country flows, then the complete dedicated suite passed 5/5. `prettier --check e2e/us03-qa.spec.ts` passed before the reruns.

## QA recommendation

The US-03 behavior passed dedicated browser, CMS integration, unit and full cross-story browser coverage. US03-QA-01 is resolved with evidence. No blocking implementation defect was reproduced. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks remain unverified.

## Findings

No blocking or non-blocking code findings.

### QA finding history

- **US03-QA-01 — Medium, resolved:** The existing US-02 browser handoff assertion expected the placeholder Summary heading. The Developer updated it to assert the implemented Summary heading, selected plan and same-country plan-change link. QA verified the correction in the full 22-test production-style Compose run.
- The QA report also records early test assertion and environment setup failures. They were corrected or avoided in the final runs and were not application findings.

## Review notes

- The terms endpoint selects published country documents only, limits the result to two to detect duplicates, projects only country and body, computes the revision from the displayed text and returns `no-store`. QA verified the Public role grants and request boundary.
- Terms are rendered through Angular interpolation. The decoder validates country, revision format, nonblank content and size before the response enters state.
- The payment command reserves the attempt synchronously by moving to `checking` before the terms refresh. Repeated activation is guarded by `canPay`, and the captured country, generation and quote snapshot are checked before processing and settlement. Navigation cancels the request/timer and invalidates late callbacks.
- The selected document is masked in the read-only review projection. The consent snapshot uses a per-country draft revision, field identifiers and kinds, selected plan ID and final price. The draft revision advances only when underlying normalized field values or kinds change, so edits to a hidden identity prefix invalidate consent even when the visible mask is unchanged.
- Receipts contain only a version, country and opaque random quote reference in bounded tab storage. Restore validates version, country and reference. The terminal receipt route bypasses editable Summary and prevents duplicate payment. Interrupted payment state and consent remain memory-only.
- Native radio controls, an associated consent label, visible feedback and a status region follow the approved design. QA exercised keyboard operation and mobile reflow.

## Recommendation

**Approved.** The reviewed changes implement the approved US-03 specification, ADR-005 and design, and QA evidence covers both countries and the complete successful and rejected payment retry flows. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast verification remain unverified for the project-level delivery record.
